Launched: £10m Internet of Things competition for UK cities
Better log on and surf the Information Super Highway to find out more about it!

I'll give my two cents...

What I believe is that the Internet of Things has come about 60+ years too late and will never be what it is touted to be. I'll explain...

The Internet of Things is, mainly, a revenue boosting system for companies. Increased knowledge of the human race and it's habits means "more taylored" adverts, products, schemes, etc. etc.. Yes, the internet of things (IOT), has the potential to improve our lives, but at what huge cost eh?

Now back to that 60 years thing. 60+ years ago consumers were much less "savvy", or knowledgable/aware of company greed and profit-chasing and advertisement and privacy invasion. The thing is, nowadays, consumers are becoming exponentially more savvy, in a way where the more savvy everybody becomes, the more savvy people want to become.

It's a positive feedback loop

The problem is IOT is only effective when people don't know how pervasive and "servaillencey" the whole thing is. The IOT only works when nobody knows what IOT really is. Once people do, people object (as they already are doing), and the whole thing collapses in lawsuits, protests, boycotts, etc. etc. etc....

I'm not sure if the opinion that I hold is what other people have, but there's my two cents.
